all.title: HippoCamp: Benchmarking Contextual Agents on Personal Computers

all.title: PerceptionComp: A Video Benchmark for Complex Perception-Centric Reasoning

all.title: Meta-Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Model Harnesses

all.title: Think, Act, Build: An Agentic Framework with Vision Language Models for Zero-Shot 3D Visual Grounding
all.summary: A dynamic agentic framework called TAB addresses 3D visual grounding by decoupling spatial semantics resolution from 3D structure instantiation through 2D VLMs and multi-view geometry, achieving superior performance over existing zero-shot and supervised methods.

all.title: MonitorBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability in Large Language Models
all.summary: MonitorBench is introduced as a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating chains of thought monitorability in large language models, revealing that monitorability decreases when structural reasoning is not required and that both open- and closed-source models exhibit reduced monitorability under stress-testing conditions.

all.title: Colon-Bench: An Agentic Workflow for Scalable Dense Lesion Annotation in Full-Procedure Colonoscopy Videos

all.title: Paper Reconstruction Evaluation: Evaluating Presentation and Hallucination in AI-written Papers
all.summary: A systematic evaluation framework called PaperRecon is proposed to assess AI-generated papers by separating quality assessment into presentation and hallucination dimensions using a benchmark of 51 recent papers.

all.title: Reasoning Shift: How Context Silently Shortens LLM Reasoning
all.summary: Reasoning behaviors in large language models compress under varied contextual conditions, potentially impacting performance on complex tasks despite maintaining accuracy on simpler ones.

all.title: ClawKeeper: Comprehensive Safety Protection for OpenClaw Agents Through Skills, Plugins, and Watchers
all.summary: OpenClaw's security vulnerabilities necessitate comprehensive protection through ClawKeeper, a real-time framework implementing skill-based, plugin-based, and watcher-based security mechanisms across multiple architectural layers.

all.title: The Model Says Walk: How Surface Heuristics Override Implicit Constraints in LLM Reasoning
all.summary: Large language models exhibit systematic reasoning failures when surface cues conflict with feasibility constraints, demonstrating consistent heuristic biases that can be measured and partially mitigated through targeted interventions.

all.title: Vision2Web: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Visual Website Development with Agent Verification
all.summary: Vision2Web presents a comprehensive benchmark for visual website development tasks and evaluates coding agents across static UI generation, interactive frontend reproduction, and full-stack development with varying complexity levels.

all.title: Dynin-Omni: Omnimodal Unified Large Diffusion Language Model
all.summary: Dynin-Omni is a novel masked-diffusion-based omnimodal foundation model that unifies text, image, speech, and video understanding and generation through a shared discrete token space, achieving superior performance across multiple multimodal benchmarks.

all.title: Brevity Constraints Reverse Performance Hierarchies in Language Models
all.summary: Large language models can underperform smaller ones due to verbose responses that introduce errors, but constraining output length reveals their superior capabilities and improves performance across benchmarks.

all.title: When Documents Disagree: Measuring Institutional Variation in Transplant Guidance with Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
all.summary: Patient education materials for solid-organ transplantation vary substantially across U.S. centers, yet no systematic method exists to quantify this heterogeneity at scale. We introduce a framework that grounds the same patient questions in different centers' handbooks using retrieval-augmented language models and compares the resulting answers using a five-label consistency taxonomy. Applied to 102 handbooks from 23 centers and 1,115 benchmark questions, the framework quantifies heterogeneity across four dimensions: question, topic, organ, and center. We find that 20.8% of non-absent pairwise comparisons exhibit clinically meaningful divergence, concentrated in condition monitoring and lifestyle topics. Coverage gaps are even more prominent: 96.2% of question-handbook pairs miss relevant content, with reproductive health at 95.1% absence. Center-level divergence profiles are stable and interpretable, where heterogeneity reflects systematic institutional differences, likely due to patient diversity. These findings expose an information gap in transplant patient education materials, with document-grounded medical question answering highlighting opportunities for content improvement.
